viva.summary: The student demonstrates a strong grasp of recursive descent parsing, correctly identifying the roles of operator precedence, token pointer management, and how to extend the grammar. They clearly understand the structural relationship between factors, terms, and expressions.

rubric.revise_next: Try implementing exponentiation next to see how you would handle right-associative operators in this recursive structure.

questions.answer: This loop makes sure that we keep adding or subtracting numbers as we go through the list of tokens. It is really important because it makes sure the calculator does the plus and minus operations in the correct order from left to right.
questions.feedback: You correctly identified that the loop handles the sequential processing of additive operators to maintain correct evaluation order.
questions.prompt: In your `parse_expr` function you have the line `while pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos] in ('+', '-'):`. What is the purpose of this loop and why is it essential for correct expression evaluation?

questions.answer: This line moves the cursor forward to the next token after processing one. We need it so the parser doesn't get stuck on the same character and keeps going through the whole input.
questions.feedback: Your explanation of the pointer increment as a mechanism to advance the parser state is spot on.
questions.prompt: Explain in your own words what this line of your code does, and why it's needed: `pos += 1`

questions.answer: I would need to modify the parse_term and p_term functions. I would add '/' to the list of operators they check for and then include a division operation in their loops just like how the multiplication logic is handled.
questions.feedback: You correctly identified that division belongs in the term-level functions alongside multiplication due to operator precedence.
